verses.zh: 耶和华的话又临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要面向西珥山发预言，攻击它，
verses.en: “Son of man, turn toward[NOTE:1] Mount Seir[NOTE:2] and prophesy against it.
notes: Mount Seir is to be identified with Edom (Ezek 35:15), home of Esau’s descendants (Gen 25:21-30).
verses.commentary:
35:2 "set your face against" See note at Ezek. 1:3.

▣ "Mount Seir" This refers to the nation of Edom (Ezek. 25:12-14; 32:29; 36:5). No other nation is listed in this context. I am
surprised that another judgment against Edom is included. She is already addressed in Ezek. 25:12-14. Edom must have a symbolic connotation. She

- mocks and attacks YHWH's people, Ezek. 35:5,11, cf. Ps. 137:7; Isa. 63:1-6; Obad. 1:8-19

- is prideful (cf. Ezek. 35:10-11), here

- has arrogant thoughts against YHWH and His people, Ezek. 35:12,13 (Edom had "everlasting enmity," Ezek. 35:5)

Moderns must admit that we do not know the reasons and procedures for the editing and compilation of OT books. It is possible
that Edom stands for all anti-God human societies (NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 957).

The concept of "mountain" may be the key to this text. The high plateau of Edom, of which they were so proud, will not save
them. As judgment came to the mountains of Israel (i.e. chapter 6), so too, now to the mountains of Edom (cf. Ezek. 35:8,15). As judgment comes
to arrogant Edom, blessing will return to the repentant covenant people (i.e. the mountains of Israel, cf. Ezek. 35:12).

Special Topic: Edom and Israel.

verses.zh: 对它说，主耶和华如此说：西珥山哪，我与你为敌，必向你伸手攻击你，使你荒凉，令人惊骇。
verses.en: Say to it, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: “‘Look, I am against you, Mount Seir;I will stretch out my hand against youand turn you into a desolate ruin.
verses.commentary:
35:3 "Lord God" This is literally "Adon YHWH."

Special Topic: Lord (adon and kurios)

Special Topic: Names for Deity, D.

▣ "I will stretch out My hand against you" This is an anthropomorphic idiom of YHWH's ability to act effectively (cf. Ezek. 25:7,13; Jer. 51:25).

Special Topic: Hand

Special Topic: God Described As Human (anthropomorphism)

▣ "a desolation and a waste" These two parallel terms (cf. Ezek. 35:7) sound alike (i.e. BDB 1031
and BDB 1031) and have the same consonants as "Shammah," a grandson of Edom (BDB 1031, cf. Gen. 36:13,17;
1 Chr. 1:37). Possible meanings are

- desolation, שׁממה, cf. Ezek. 35:4,7,9,14,15

- waste, משׁמה, cf. Ezek. 35:7; 6:14; 33:28,29

- a grandson of Edom, שׁמה

verses.zh: 我必使你的城邑变为荒场，成为凄凉。你就知道我是耶和华。
verses.en: I will lay waste your cities,and you will become desolate.Then you will know that I am the Lord!

verses.zh: 因为你永怀仇恨，在以色列人遭灾、罪孽到了尽头的时候，将他们交与刀剑，
verses.en: “‘You have shown unrelenting hostility and poured the people of Israel onto the blades of a sword[NOTE:1] at the time of their calamity, at the time of their final punishment.
notes: Or “gave over…to the power of the sword.” This phrase also occurs in Jer 18:21 and Ps 63:10.
verses.commentary:
35:5 "everlasting enmity" This is a good exaple where the Hebrew term 'olam (everlasting) cannot have an
eternal meaning. Judah's judgment was necessary, deserved, complete, but not eternal.

Special Topic: Forever ('olam and aiōnios)

▣ "sons of Israel" This is usiing "Israel" in its collective sense. The context is primarily addressing Judah.

▣ "at the time of their calamity, at the time of the punishment of the end" Notice that these two phrases are parallel. The first obviously
refers to the invasion of Judah by Neo-Babylon. The second must refer to the same time, which shows "the end" (BDB 893). Interpreters must be careful
of not assigning one meaning to a word or phrase and then using it in every place the word appears. Context determines meaning, not one's systematic eschatology!

verses.zh: 所以主耶和华说：我指着我的永生起誓，我必使你遭遇流血的报应，罪（原文是血；本节同）必追赶你；你既不恨恶杀人流血，所以这罪必追赶你。
verses.en: Therefore, as surely as I live, declares the Sovereign Lord, I will subject you to bloodshed, and bloodshed will pursue you. Since you did not hate bloodshed, bloodshed will pursue you.
verses.commentary:
35:6 "as I live" This is an oath based on the name of YHWH, the ever-living, only-living, I Am (cf. Exod. 3:14). This is a recurrent idiom in
Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 5:11; 14:16,18,20; 16:48; 17:16,19; 18:3; 20:3,31; 33:11; 34:8; 35:6,11).

Special Topic: Names for Deity, D.

▣ "blood" The term (BDB 196) can refer to one's "life force" and if it is spilt, to one's death. It is used four times in this verse.

- I will give you over to bloodshed

- bloodshed will pursue you

- you have not hated bloodshed (i.e. murder)

- therefore, bloodshed will pursue you (repeated)

We reap what we sow (cf. Ezek. 35:11,15).

Just a textual note, the LXX changes #3 to "you are guilty of blood," which is followed by RSV,
NEB, REB, NJB, but this demands a change of several consonants. The MT makes sense.

The UBS Text project, p. 120, suggests that #3 uses "blood" as a reference to Edom's kinsmen, Judah. It, like the NASB,
adds the negative "not," which is missing in the MT. It was not Edom's violence (cf. Jer. 49:7-22) but her disregard for kinship that caused YHWH's wrath.

verses.zh: 我必使西珥山荒凉，令人惊骇，来往经过的人我必剪除。
verses.en: I will turn Mount Seir into a desolate ruin;[NOTE:1] I will cut off[NOTE:2] from it the one who passes through or returns.
notes: The translation reads with some manuscripts לְשִׁמְמָה וּמְשַׁמָּה (leshimemah umeshammah, “desolate ruin”) as in verse 3 and often in Ezekiel. The majority reading reverses the first mem (מ) with the shin (שׁ), resulting in the repetition of the word desolate: לְשִׁמְמָה וּשְׁמָמָה (leshimemah ushemamah).
verses.commentary: 35:7 Mount Seir is an idiom for all the inhabitants of Edom (i.e. v. 15).

verses.zh: 我必使西珥山满有被杀的人。被刀杀的，必倒在你小山和山谷，并一切的溪水中。
verses.en: I will fill its mountains with its dead; on your hills and in your valleys and in all your ravines, those killed by the sword will fall.

verses.zh: 我必使你永远荒凉，使你的城邑无人居住，你的民就知道我是耶和华。
verses.en: I will turn you into a perpetual desolation, and your cities will not be inhabited. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
verses.commentary:
35:9 Edom's destruction will be permanent (cf. Mal. 1:2-4, esp. Ezek. 35:4; Jer. 49:13). Edom's permanent
destruction was because of her "everlasting enmity" (Ezek. 35:5; and Obadiah)!

verses.zh: 因为你曾说：『这二国这二邦必归于我，我必得为业』（其实耶和华仍在那里），
verses.en: “‘You said, “These two nations, these two lands[NOTE:1] will be mine, and we will possess them,”[NOTE:2] (although the Lord was there);
notes: The reference is to Israel and Judah.
verses.commentary:
35:10 Edom rejected its required brotherly love for Judah (and Israel, i.e. "two nations") and desired her lands for herself (cf. Ezek. 35:5, 10). The problem
is that Judah's land belonged to YHWH (i.e. "the Lord was there"). It was only Judah's by a conditional covenant.

YHWH left Judah in chapter 10, but in Ezek. 48:35 the book of Ezekiel ends with "The YHWH is there" (cf. Ps. 132:13,14).

Special Topic: Edom and Israel

Special Topic: Covenant

verses.zh: 所以主耶和华说：我指着我的永生起誓，我必照你的怒气和你从仇恨中向他们所发的嫉妒待你。我审判你的时候，必将自己显明在他们中间。
verses.en: therefore, as surely as I live, declares the Sovereign Lord, I will deal with you according to your anger and your envy, by which you acted spitefully against them. I will reveal myself to them when I judge you.

verses.zh: 你也必知道我―耶和华听见了你的一切毁谤，就是你攻击以色列山的话，说：『这些山荒凉，是归我们吞灭的。』
verses.en: Then you will know that I, the Lord, have heard all the insults you spoke against the mountains of Israel, saying, “They are desolate; they have been given to us for food.”
verses.commentary:
35:12

NASB
"revilings"

NKJV, NJB, REB, LXX, Peshitta
"blasphemies"

NRSV
"abusive speech"

TEV
"with contempt"

JPSOA
"taunts"

NET
"insults"

The NOUN (BDB 611, KB 658) is found only here and Neh. 9:18. The revilings are against "the mountains
of Israel," but clearly, in context, it is against Israel's God (cf. Ezek. 35:5,10-11,13). This is why Edom is often seen as a type of all anti-God nations!

verses.zh: 你们也用口向我夸大，增添与我反对的话，我都听见了。
verses.en: You exalted yourselves against me with your speech[NOTE:1] and hurled many insults against me[NOTE:2]—I have heard them all!
notes: Heb “and you multiplied against me your words.” The Hebrew verb occurs only here and in Prov 27:6, where it refers to the “excessive” kisses of an enemy. The basic idea of the verb appears to be “to be abundant.” Here it occurs in the causative (Hiphil) stem.

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：全地欢乐的时候，我必使你荒凉。
verses.en: This is what the Sovereign Lord says: While the whole earth rejoices, I will turn you into a desolation.
verses.commentary:
35:14 "as all the earth rejoices" This is hyperbolic imagery. The earth, as YHWH's creation, rejoices
when His will is done. The earth is affected by humanity's sin (cf. Genesis 3; Rom. 8:19-22).

Special Topic: Land, Country, Earth (OT)

verses.zh: 你怎样因以色列家的地业荒凉而喜乐，我必照你所行的待你。西珥山哪，你和以东全地必都荒凉。你们就知道我是耶和华。」
verses.en: As you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel because it was desolate, so will I deal with you—you will be desolate, Mount Seir, and all Edom—all of it! Then they will know that I am the Lord.’”

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the four modern translations above.
Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.
